speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; to better understand its cause, how long has it been present and what does it look like? Did you have any recent blood tests done to check your blood sugar levels?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Venous Leg Ulcer (secondary to prior DVT and familial predisposition to venous disease).

The history of a 10-year chronic swelling, a previous DVT, and a strong family history points strongly to venous insufficiency. Given the wound has been present for 6 months, I need to confirm the extent of the ulceration and rule out infection. REQUEST IMAGES: Right lower leg wound and venous duplex ultrasound.
